[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

In the adjoining figure, \(CD\) is the diameter of a semicircle with center \(O.\) Point \(A\) lies on the extension of \(DC\) past \(C;\) point \(E\) lies on the semicircle, and \(B\) is the point of intersection (distinct from \(E\)) of line segment \(AE\) with the semicircle. If line segments \(AB\) and \(CD\) may be rotated about points \(B\) and \(C,\) respectively, so that points \(A\) and \(D\) coincide, to form a triangle with positive area, then which of the following three inequalities must be satisfied? \[ \begin{aligned} &\text{I. }x\lt\frac z2\\ &\text{II. }y\lt x+\frac z2\\ &\text{III. }y\lt\frac z2 \end{aligned} \]

mappings.rationale: The square and equilateral triangle give AD=AE and determine their included angle. Equal base angles in triangle ADE then determine the requested angle.
mappings.answerReason: AD=AB=AE, and the exterior placement gives ∠DAE=90°+60°=150°. Thus triangle ADE is isosceles and ∠AED=(180°−150°)/2=15°.

mappings.rationale: AB=OB makes triangle AOB isosceles, while OB=OE makes triangle BOE isosceles. Their base-angle relations combine with the straight-line supplements.
mappings.answerReason: Let x=∠BAO. Since AB=OB, ∠AOB=x and ∠ABO=180°−2x. Collinearity of A,B,E gives ∠OBE=2x, so ∠BEO=2x. Also ∠AOE=180°−45°=135°. Triangle AOE therefore gives x+2x+135°=180°, hence x=15°.

mappings.rationale: Rotation preserves the three lengths x, y−x, and z−y. Positive area requires all three strict triangle inequalities.
mappings.answerReason: The triangle inequalities give x+(y−x)>z−y, x+(z−y)>y−x, and (y−x)+(z−y)>x. These simplify to y>z/2, y<x+z/2, and x<z/2. Thus I and II hold, while III is false.

mappings.rationale: Perpendicular-distance lower bounds show that the connector of the opposite edge midpoints is shortest. Spatial coordinates alternatively express the squared distance as a constant plus two nonnegative squares.
mappings.answerReason: Let M,N be the midpoints of AB,CD. The equilateral faces give CM=DM=√3/2 and AB perpendicular to plane CDM. Hence PQ≥MQ≥MN. Since MN is perpendicular to CD, MN²=CM²−CN²=3/4−1/4=1/2. Equality occurs at P=M and Q=N, so the minimum is √2/2.

mappings.rationale: Each equal-radius intersection lies on the perpendicular bisector of its two centers. Pythagoras determines its offset from the midpoint, and symmetry with 30° projections determines B'C'.
mappings.answerReason: For the labeled outer intersections, let h=√(r²−1), their distance from the respective midpoints of AC and AB. Those midpoints are 1 apart. Symmetry makes B'C' parallel to BC, and each outward offset contributes a projection (√3/2)h. Therefore B'C'=1+√3h=1+√(3(r²−1)).
limitations: For 1<r<2/√3, both intersections of a pair of circles lie outside the third circle, so the outside-circle wording alone is nonunique. The labeled outer intersections in the supplied figure are used.

mappings.rationale: The two 80° angles give CD=CE=BC/2. Base and height ratios express the requested sum using the area of ABC; an auxiliary similar triangle and the cosine law at 60° determine its exact value.
mappings.answerReason: Write a=BC and c=AB. Choose X on AC with ∠ABX=20°. Then CX=a, and similarity of ABX and ACB gives 1−a=c². The cosine law gives a²=1+c²−c, hence c(a+2)=1. Also CD=CE=a/2, so [CDE]=a[ABC]/4. Since [ABC]=√3c/4, the requested sum is √3c(a+2)/8=√3/8.

mappings.rationale: The two square angles and the equilateral-triangle angle occupy three sectors around D. Subtracting them from a full turn gives the remaining angle.
mappings.answerReason: The displayed sectors ∠ADC, ∠CDE, and ∠EDG measure 90°, 60°, and 90°. Thus ∠GDA=360°−90°−60°−90°=120°.

mappings.rationale: The perpendicular diameters make triangle PQC right at Q, and QC=AQ because both are radii. The 60° tangent ratio determines the requested leg ratio.
mappings.answerReason: In right triangle PQC, tan 60°=QC/PQ=√3. Since QC=AQ, PQ/AQ=1/√3=√3/3.
